subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should Telegram fresh setup switch from pairing to token-verified owner allowlist capture, and what compatibility semantics should existing implicit or explicit pairing configs keep?
rationale: This changes Telegram first-run trust and default authorization rather than repairing a broken documented contract, and the safe implementation depends on maintainer intent for onboarding, upgrade, and security behavior.

options.title: Token-Verified Fresh Setup Default
options.body: Generate a setup token, require the intended owner to send it to the bot, then write dmPolicy="allowlist" and allowFrom for fresh Telegram setups while preserving explicit pairing configs.

options.title: Keep Pairing Default
options.body: Leave pairing as the default and improve warnings/docs, accepting the current pairing-request exposure as the chosen first-run tradeoff.

options.title: Defer To Cross-Channel Auto-Flip
options.body: Handle this only through the broader post-bootstrap default-flip discussion in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/81876, leaving first-run Telegram setup unchanged.

recommendation.title: Token-Verified Fresh Setup Default
recommendation.body: Generate a setup token, require the intended owner to send it to the bot, then write dmPolicy="allowlist" and allowFrom for fresh Telegram setups while preserving explicit pairing configs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent history across Telegram docs/runtime access and already left detailed maintainer-facing review context on this issue.
